clue.text: Think logically about a boy

parts.note: re is Latin-derived 'concerning'
taken as written
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to think clearly about a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to work something out by logical thought, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Stop female artist wearing check

indicators.note: the check is worn around the female artist like clothing, so it goes outside

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
F is the standard abbreviation for female
RA, Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A woman painter dressed in a checked garment is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a pattern on clothing, which suits 'wearing', but here it means restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, a verb synonym for stop.

clue.text: Reptile flying at gorilla

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A reptile launches itself at a gorilla, a jungle brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian, so an example of the reptile class.

clue.text: Lazy old couple housing sailor

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a word that houses another holds it inside itself

parts.note: to couple is to tie together
OS, ordinary seaman, a crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An idle elderly pair give a seaman lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a noun for a pair of people; it is the verb meaning to join.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means idle or serving no purpose; its older sense is indolent, at leisure.

clue.text: Fruit in orchard's first row

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of orchard
a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Fruit growing in the front row of an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Where you can see clock's hands, apparently

definitions.text: Where you can see clock's hands
definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: the hands are on a clock's dial

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is read literally: a clock's hands sit on its dial, the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means superficially or to judge from appearances, the same as apparently.

clue.text: Last, at the end of the day

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming behind everyone else

definitions.text: at the end of the day
definitions.meaning: second meaning: when everything is considered

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase means following everybody, hence last; idiomatically it means in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both meanings are idioms: behind every other person, and ultimately or when all is said and done.

clue.text: Good scope for stable hand

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
room is scope or latitude, as in room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A promising opportunity for someone working with horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom looks after horses, so a worker in a stable.

clue.text: Charging Victoria, say, where juice is sold

parts.note: charging a glass or tank is filling it
Victoria is a London railway station, the 'say' marking it as an example

explanation.surface: A London terminus charging for a place selling fruit juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juice' is slang for fuel, so the definition is a petrol station, not a drinks stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling station is a petrol station, the place motorists buy fuel, called juice in slang.

clue.text: How, stoically, to suffer the unwanted paparazzi?

parts.words: How, stoically, to suffer the unwanted paparazzi?
parts.note: surface reading: advice on putting up with intrusive photographers
setter's reading: the photographers want a smile and some bare flesh, so the phrase puns on bare

explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase for enduring something cheerfully sounds like smiling and stripping, which is exactly what paparazzi want.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to put up with an unpleasant situation patiently, which is how stoics suffer.

clue.text: Painter having year in part of India

indicators.note: a place having something in it holds it within

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An artist spends a year in a region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter, an example of the class.

clue.text: Friar of noble birth in Spain

parts.note: august means venerable or of noble standing
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A monk of aristocratic family living in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: An Augustine is a friar of the Augustinian order, named after St Augustine.

clue.text: Codeword, more used in front of 'Oscar'

indicators.note: placing one part ahead of another fixes their order in the answer
something used has been worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Oscar is the NATO phonetic codeword for the letter O

explanation.surface: Radio etiquette: one codeword is used more often before another.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Oscar' another codeword in a sequence; it only supplies its letter, O, placed after the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is the NATO phonetic alphabet's codeword for the letter R.

clue.text: Comment in memo

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a short written message

explanation.walkthrough: The two nouns are joined by 'in', which reads as a comment inside a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is both a brief remark or observation and a short written reminder or message.

clue.text: Cabal can, as represented in film

indicators.note: to represent is to present anew, so the letters are set out afresh

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A secret clique can be depicted on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is the 1942 Bogart and Bergman film, an example of the category.

clue.text: After noon, clear up after Brown in his former home?

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon
umber is a brown earth pigment

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to clear a sum is to net it as profit

explanation.surface: Tidying up Gordon Brown's old residence in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown does double duty: the colour gives letters, and Gordon Brown, former Prime Minister, owns the former home. 'After' twice sets the order: UMBER after N, then the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten Downing Street is the Prime Minister's residence, so Gordon Brown's home while in office.

clue.text: Enterprising sort making torte with egg, whisked

indicators.note: whisking ingredients mixes them up, so the letters are stirred

parts.note: torte plus egg, 'with' joining them, are the eight letters

explanation.surface: An ambitious baker makes a cake with whipped egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is an ambitious, energetic person, someone with drive and initiative.

clue.text: Governor taking in surprisingly modern small London district

indicators.note: the governor takes the rest inside himself

parts.note: a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement is an unexpected one, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: modern plus S, the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An official takes in a little part of London that is unexpectedly up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: BERMONDSEY is a district of south-east London, by the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermondsey is an area in the London borough of Southwark, so an example of a London district.

clue.text: Second defender

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to support, as in seconding a motion
second meaning: a defensive player in football or hockey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number or a unit of time, but here it is the verb to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal is to second it, and a back is a defensive position in team sports.

clue.text: Novel set in Salem, Massachusetts

indicators.note: something set in these words is embedded among their letters

parts.note: runs across the end of the town and the start of the state

explanation.surface: A novel with its story located in a famous New England town.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's 1815 novel, an example of the class.

clue.text: Intricately traced round in style of interior design

indicators.note: intricate work twists and weaves, so the letters are interlaced afresh

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A circular pattern finely drawn in a decorative style.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the bold geometric style of the 1920s and 30s, used in buildings and interiors.

clue.text: Charge way over the odds for wool

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the odds' is a British idiom for more than the proper price.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is slang for to rip someone off, and a fleece is the woolly coat shorn from a sheep.

clue.text: Clubs suffer defeat nearby

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to lose is to suffer defeat

explanation.surface: Local football clubs are beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as an adverb means near at hand, the same sense as nearby.

clue.text: Greek character making an appearance in home game

indicators.note: the answer shows itself inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Greek player features in a match at his club's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in the game, but it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Leader in event to head into the wind on the way back — man is brilliant

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of event

indicators.note: travelling back means going in the opposite direction, right to left

parts.note: to luff is a sailing term for steering a boat closer into the wind
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man who sails expertly into the wind on the return leg of a race is brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Effulgent means shining brightly, radiant, the literal sense of brilliant.

clue.text: Reprimand rep in hall

parts.note: to lecture someone is to scold them
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A sales rep is told off in a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rep' looks like a sales representative; it is a repertory company, a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture theatre is a tiered university hall for giving lectures.

clue.text: Mimic arrives on board vessel

indicators.note: a passenger on board a vessel is inside it

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: An impersonator gets onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which makes 'on board' read naturally; here it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as the talking bird does, which is to mimic.

clue.text: Slowly fencing in a shed

indicators.note: a fence encloses what it surrounds, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gradually putting a fence around a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof resting on that wall.
